readall_conflicts: No direct source conflict, because the one listed work is a grammar of Akabea, not Akar-Bale, and the catalog's Akar-Bale record ('weight-hedged', empty rule, no quote) cites no readable source. Indirectly there is tension: Zamponi & Comrie (2020: 58-59) establish fixed root-initial stress for the sister language Akabea from Temple (1877: 9) and from Portman's (1898: 29) convention that unmarked words are first-syllable stressed, a convention Portman applied across his South Andaman comparative vocabulary (which includes Akarbale) while marking stress only on a few Okol and Okojuwoi items. That points toward root-initial (morphological) stress for Akar-Bale as well, not a weight-sensitive system; the catalog's weight-hedged entry has no support in anything opened here.

audit.recode_to: (conditional) set by morphology / root-initial, non-weight-sensitive — only if Zamponi & Comrie 2020 ch. 2 analyses Portman's stress marks as root-initial without long-vowel attraction; otherwise keep weight-sensitive (tentative).

sources.citation: Portman, M. V. 1898. Notes on the Languages of the South Andaman Group of Tribes. Calcutta: Government Printing. page scan pp. 29-30 from archive.org (notesonlanguage00portgoog, leaves n43-n44).
sources.quote: 'A line is placed under a syllable to show the stress on it. When a word is not so marked the stress should be placed on the first syllable. In the vocabulary where words are used with hyphens or affixes, the ROOT is printed in italics.' Then Akar-Bale-specific notes: 'The Bálé language has a peculiar lingual, thick, t ... The long á with this tribe is always pronounced as if preceded by a very short o. O is the distinguishing vowel of the Bálé language'.
sources.note: Portman underlines stressed non-initial syllables word by word in Akar-Bale forms; the underlines are lost in the scanned text we hold layer. Inspecting the scans would give direct Akarbale evidence on whether long vowels attract stress off the root-initial syllable (Temple's claim) — the only language-specific stress data that exists. Two statement pages (29-30) downloaded now; the vocabulary leaves were not.
